tagline: Down the Missouri bank, from Twain's town to New Madrid.
intro: The river road keeps to the Missouri bank of the Mississippi, down past Canton and Hannibal, Louisiana and Elsberry, past St. Charles, where the Missouri River comes in, and the Arch at St. Louis, then on south through Ste. Genevieve and Cape Girardeau to New Madrid.

Several of the towns along it were French or Spanish before they were American. New Madrid started as a trading post where hunters processed bear and buffalo fat for working skins and furs, and was known for it as L'Anse a la Graise, the Cove of Grease.

moments.title: Hannibal
moments.text: Mark Twain's boyhood town keeps the cave that inspired Tom and Becky's getting lost, Lover's Leap above the river, and a memorial lighthouse of 1933 that three presidents have lit.

moments.title: Ste. Genevieve
moments.text: After the flood of 1785 moved the town two miles north and half a mile inland, it built its houses of upright wooden posts, and three of the nation's five surviving posts-in-the-ground houses stand here.

moments.title: New Madrid
moments.text: In February 1812 the earthquake that destroyed the town raised the ground at Kentucky Bend enough to put temporary waterfalls on the Mississippi.
